long_biography.plain_text:
Before building a regional media company, Hani Jabsheh spent two years broking energy risks for Aon at Lloyd's in London. He had studied business administration at Wilfrid Laurier University, and the combination of finance training and cross-border work led him toward the Arab world's emerging internet economy. In 2000 he co-founded Al Bawaba in Amman.

Jabsheh developed the company around both publishing and infrastructure. Its bilingual news operation created a direct audience, while SyndiGate licensed and distributed content for publishers, databases, governments and brands. The model turned regional reporting into a broader information business with offices and clients beyond Jordan. Alongside the media group, Jabsheh served as a non-executive director of his family's International General Insurance business, connecting entrepreneurship with an older family insurance tradition. His newer work at Kamanga applies his experience in licensing and intellectual property to data provenance and rights management.
